title.zh: 卷十八 列傳第十二: 沈眾 袁泌 劉仲威 陸山才 王質 韋載
title.en: Volume 18: Shen Zhong; Yuan mi; Liu Zhongwei; Lu Shancai; Wang Zhi); Wei Zai
title.raw: 卷十八 列傳第十二: 沈眾 袁泌 劉仲威 陸山才 王質 韋載 Volume 18: Shen Zhong; Yuan mi; Liu Zhongwei; Lu Shancai; Wang Zhi); Wei Zai

sentences.zh: 陳書卷十八

translations.literal: Book of Chen, Volume 18
translations.idiomatic: Book of Chen, Volume 18

sentences.zh: 列傳第十二

translations.literal: Biographies, Number Twelve
translations.idiomatic: Biographies, Part Twelve

sentences.zh: 沈眾 袁泌 劉仲威 陸山才 王質 韋載 族弟翽

translations.literal: Shen Zhong; Yuan Bi; Liu Zhongwei; Lu Shancai; Wang Zhi; Wei Zai; younger clansman Hui
translations.idiomatic: Shen Zhong; Yuan Bi; Liu Zhongwei; Lu Shancai; Wang Zhi; Wei Zai; younger clansman Hui

sentences.zh: 沈眾字仲師，吳興武康人也。

translations.literal: Shen Zhong, styled Zhongshi, was a native of Wukang in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Zhong, styled Zhongshi, was a native of Wukang in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 祖約，梁特進。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yue was Liang Special Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yue had been Liang's special grand master.

sentences.zh: 父旋，梁給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: His father Xuan was Liang Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xuan was an attendant gentleman of the Yellow Gate under Liang.

sentences.zh: 眾好學，頗有文詞，起家梁鎮衛南平王法曹參軍、太子舍人。

translations.literal: Zhong loved learning and had considerable literary skill; he began his career as Registrar to the Prince of Nanping of the Garrison Guard and Household Retainer to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong loved study and wrote well. He entered service as registrar to the Prince of Nanping of the garrison guard and as household retainer to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 是時，梁武帝制千字詩，眾為之注解。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Wu of Liang composed the Thousand-Character Poem, and Zhong wrote a commentary on it.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Liang composed the Thousand-Character Poem, Zhong annotated it.

sentences.zh: 與陳郡謝景同時召見于文德殿，帝令眾為竹賦，賦成，奏，帝善之，手敕答曰：[1]「卿文體翩翩，可謂無忝爾祖。

translations.literal: He and Xie Jing of Chen commandery were summoned together to the Wende Hall; the Emperor ordered Zhong to compose a bamboo rhapsody; when it was finished he presented it; the Emperor praised it and replied by hand-edict: Editorial footnote marker 1. "Your literary style is light and graceful—you truly do no dishonor to your ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: He and Xie Jing of Chen were summoned together to the Wende Hall. The emperor ordered Zhong to write a rhapsody on bamboo; when it was done he presented it, and the emperor praised it and wrote back in his own hand: [1] "Your style flows lightly—you truly do no dishonor to your ancestor.

sentences.zh: 」當陽公蕭大心為郢州刺史，以眾為限內記室參軍。

translations.literal: " The Duke of Dangyang, Xiao Daxin, was made Inspector of Yingzhou and appointed Zhong Recorder within the commandery limits.
translations.idiomatic: " The Duke of Dangyang, Xiao Daxin, became inspector of Yingzhou and made Zhong his recorder within the commandery limits.

sentences.zh: 尋除鎮南湘東王記室參軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was removed and made Recorder to the Prince of Xiangdong, Pacifier of the South.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to recorder to the Prince of Xiangdong, pacifier of the south.

sentences.zh: 遷太子中舍人，兼散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Household Retainer in the Heir Apparent's palace, concurrently Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to household retainer in the heir's palace and was concurrently made regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 聘魏，還，遷驃騎廬陵王諮議參軍，舍人如故。

translations.literal: On embassy to Wei he returned and was made Adviser to the Prince of Luling of the Flying Cavalry and kept his post as retainer.
translations.idiomatic: After an embassy to Wei he was made adviser to the Prince of Luling of the flying cavalry, retaining his post as retainer.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，眾表於梁武，稱家代所隸故義部曲，並在吳興，求還召募以討賊，梁武許之。

translations.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion Zhong memorialized Emperor Wu of Liang, saying that the righteous household troops his family had long commanded were all in Wuxing, and asked to return to recruit them to attack the rebel; Emperor Wu approved.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion Zhong memorialized Emperor Wu of Liang, saying the loyal household troops his line had long commanded were in Wuxing, and asked leave to return and raise them against the rebel. The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 及景圍臺城，[2]眾率宗族及義附五千餘人，入援京邑，頓于小航，對賊東府置陣，軍容甚整，景深憚之。

translations.literal: When Jing besieged the Terrace City, Editorial footnote marker 2. Zhong led his clansmen and volunteer followers—more than five thousand men—to reinforce the capital, encamped at Little Ferry, and drew up battle lines opposite the rebel Eastern Mansion; his army's bearing was very orderly, and Jing deeply feared him.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing besieged the Terrace City, [2] Zhong led his kinsmen and volunteer followers—more than five thousand men—to relieve the capital. He encamped at Little Ferry and formed ranks opposite the rebels' Eastern Mansion. His troops were tightly arrayed, and Jing feared him greatly.

sentences.zh: 梁武於城內遙授眾為太子右衛率。

translations.literal: From within the city Emperor Wu of Liang remotely appointed Zhong Right Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard.
translations.idiomatic: From within the city Emperor Wu of Liang appointed Zhong right commandant of the heir's guard by remote commission.

sentences.zh: 京城陷，眾降於景。

translations.literal: When the capital fell, Zhong surrendered to Jing.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell, Zhong surrendered to Jing.

sentences.zh: 景平，西上荊州，元帝以為太子中庶子、本州大中正。

translations.literal: When Jing was pacified, Zhong went west to Jingzhou; Emperor Yuan of Liang made him Household Retainer to the Heir Apparent and Grand Arbiter of his native province.
translations.idiomatic: After Jing was suppressed, Zhong went west to Jingzhou. Emperor Yuan of Liang made him household retainer to the heir apparent and grand arbiter of his native province.

sentences.zh: 尋遷司徒左長史。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Left Chief Clerk of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to left chief clerk of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 江陵陷，為西魏所虜，尋而逃還，敬帝承制，授御史中丞。

translations.literal: When Jiangling fell he was taken captive by Western Wei; soon he escaped and returned; Emperor Jing of Liang under the provisional regime appointed him Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling fell he was captured by Western Wei, but soon escaped. Emperor Jing of Liang, under the provisional regime, made him censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 紹泰元年，除侍中，遷左民尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaotai he was made Palace Attendant and promoted to Master of the Left for the People.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaotai (555) he was made palace attendant and promoted to master of the left for the people.

sentences.zh: 高祖受命，遷中書令，中正如故。

translations.literal: When the Founder received the Mandate, Zhong was made Director of the Secretariat, grand arbiter unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder took the throne, Zhong was made director of the Secretariat, retaining his post as grand arbiter.

sentences.zh: 高祖以眾州里知名，甚敬重之，賞賜優渥，超於時輩。

translations.literal: Because Zhong was renowned in the Founder's home region, the Founder greatly respected him, favored him with generous gifts, and treated him above his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder, knowing Zhong's name in his own country, honored him deeply, heaped gifts on him, and favored him above his peers.

sentences.zh: 眾性吝嗇，內治產業，財帛以億計，無所分遺。

translations.literal: Zhong was by nature miserly; inwardly he built up estates, and his wealth in coin and silk ran to hundreds of millions, yet he shared nothing with others.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong was miserly by nature. He amassed estates at home until his wealth in coin and silk reached hundreds of millions, yet gave nothing away.

sentences.zh: 其自奉養甚薄，每於朝會之中，衣裳破裂，或躬提冠屨。

translations.literal: He supported himself very meagerly; at court assemblies his clothes were often torn, and sometimes he carried his own cap and shoes.
translations.idiomatic: He lived on almost nothing. At court his robes were often in tatters, and sometimes he carried his own cap and shoes.

sentences.zh: 永定二年，兼起部尚書，監起太極殿。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongding he was concurrently made Minister of Works for Construction and supervised the building of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongding (558) he was concurrently made minister of works for construction and oversaw the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 恆服布袍芒屩，以麻繩為帶，又攜乾魚蔬菜飯獨噉之，朝士共誚其所為。

translations.literal: He always wore a cloth robe and straw sandals, used hemp rope for a belt, and carried dried fish and vegetables for his lone meal; court gentlemen together mocked his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He always wore a cloth robe and straw sandals, bound himself with a hemp cord, and ate dried fish and vegetables alone. The gentlemen at court mocked him for it.

sentences.zh: [3]眾性狷急，於是忿恨，遂歷詆公卿，非毀朝廷。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 3. Zhong was by nature narrow and quick-tempered; thereupon in resentment he went through the ranks slandering the dukes and ministers and reviling the court.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial footnote marker 3. Zhong was narrow and hot-tempered. Stung by the mockery, he turned on the court, slandering dukes and ministers and reviling the government.

sentences.zh: 高祖大怒，以眾素有令望，不欲顯誅之，後因其休假還武康，遂於吳中賜死，時年五十六。

translations.literal: The Founder was greatly angered; because Zhong had long enjoyed a fine reputation, he did not wish to execute him openly; later, on a leave to return to Wukang, he was ordered to take his own life in Wu, aged fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder was furious. Because Zhong still enjoyed a fine name, he would not kill him openly; later, when Zhong took leave to return to Wukang, he was ordered to die by his own hand in Wu. He was fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 袁泌字文洋，左光祿大夫敬之弟也。

translations.literal: Yuan Bi, styled Wenyang, was the younger brother of Left Grand Master of the Golden Sigil Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Bi, styled Wenyang, was the younger brother of left grand master of the golden sigil Jing.

sentences.zh: 清正有幹局，容體魁岸，志行脩謹。

translations.literal: Upright and pure, with administrative capacity, of imposing stature, and careful in conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He was upright and capable, tall in bearing, and scrupulous in conduct.

sentences.zh: 釋褐員外散騎侍郎，歷諸王府佐。

translations.literal: He doffed the commoner's garb as Supernumerary Regular Attendant and served as aide in several princely establishments.
translations.idiomatic: He left the commoner's dress for supernumerary regular attendant and served as aide in several princely households.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，泌欲求為將。

translations.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion Bi wished to become a general.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion Bi sought a military command.

sentences.zh: 是時泌兄君正為吳郡太守，梁簡文板泌為東宮領直，令往吳中召募士卒。

translations.literal: At that time Bi's elder brother Junzheng was Administrator of Wu commandery; Emperor Jianwen of Liang commissioned Bi as Leader of Direct Service in the Eastern Palace and ordered him to Wu to recruit soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: At that time his elder brother Junzheng was administrator of Wu commandery. Emperor Jianwen of Liang commissioned Bi as leader of direct service in the eastern palace and sent him to Wu to raise troops.

sentences.zh: 及景圍臺城，泌率所領赴援。

translations.literal: When Jing besieged the Terrace City, Bi led the men under his command to the relief.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing besieged the Terrace City, Bi led his command to the relief.

sentences.zh: 京城陷，退保東陽，景使兵追之，乃自會稽東嶺出湓城，依于鄱陽嗣王蕭範。

translations.literal: When the capital fell he withdrew to hold Dongyang; Jing sent troops in pursuit, and he went out by the eastern pass of Kuaiji through Tangcheng and attached himself to the Heir of Poyang, Xiao Fan.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell he fell back to Dongyang. Jing sent troops after him; Bi slipped out by the eastern pass of Kuaiji through Tangcheng and joined the heir of Poyang, Xiao Fan.

sentences.zh: 範卒，泌乃降景。

translations.literal: When Fan died, Bi thereupon surrendered to Jing.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan died, Bi surrendered to Jing.

sentences.zh: 景平，王僧辯表泌為富春太守，兼丹陽尹。

translations.literal: When Jing was pacified, Wang Sengbian memorialized that Bi be made Administrator of Fuchun, concurrently Intendant of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Jing was suppressed, Wang Sengbian recommended Bi as administrator of Fuchun and intendant of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 貞陽侯僭位，以泌為侍中，奉使於齊。

translations.literal: When the Marquis of Zhenyang usurped the throne, Bi was made Palace Attendant and sent on embassy to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When the Marquis of Zhenyang seized the throne, Bi was made palace attendant and sent as envoy to Qi.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，王琳據有上流，泌自齊從梁永嘉王蕭莊達琳所。

translations.literal: When the Founder received the abdication, Wang Lin held the upper reaches; Bi came from Qi with Liang's Prince of Yongjia, Xiao Zhuang, to Lin's camp.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder took the throne, Wang Lin held the upper Yangzi. Bi came from Qi with Liang's Prince of Yongjia, Xiao Zhuang, to join Lin.

sentences.zh: 及莊僭立，[4]以泌為侍中、丞相長史。

translations.literal: When Zhuang usurped the throne, Editorial footnote marker 4. Bi was made Palace Attendant and Chief Clerk to the Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuang declared himself emperor, [4] Bi was made palace attendant and chief clerk to the chancellor.

sentences.zh: [5]天嘉二年，泌與琳輔莊至于柵口，琳軍敗，[6]眾皆奔散，唯泌獨乘輕舟送莊達于北境，屬莊於御史中丞劉仲威，令共入齊，然後拜辭而歸，詣闕請罪，文帝深義之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiancheng, Bi with Lin escorted Zhuang to Zhakou; Lin's army was defeated; Editorial footnote marker 6. the troops all scattered; only Bi alone took a light boat and saw Zhuang to the northern border, entrusted Zhuang to Censor-in-Chief Liu Zhongwei, and had them enter Qi together; then he took leave and returned, came to the court to confess guilt, and Emperor Wen deeply approved his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tiancheng (561), Bi and Lin escorted Zhuang to Zhakou. Lin's army was broken; [6] the troops fled in all directions. Bi alone took a light boat, saw Zhuang to the northern frontier, and placed him in the care of censor-in-chief Liu Zhongwei to enter Qi together. Then he bowed farewell, returned, and presented himself to confess fault. Emperor Wen held his conduct in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 劉仲威

translations.literal: Liu Zhongwei
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhongwei

sentences.zh: 劉仲威南陽涅陽人也。

translations.literal: Liu Zhongwei was a native of Niyang in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhongwei was a native of Niyang in Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 祖虯，齊世以國子博士徵，不就。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qiu in Qi times was summoned as Erudite of the National University and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qiu, in Qi times, was summoned as erudite of the national university and declined.

sentences.zh: 父之遴，荊州治中從事史。

translations.literal: His father Zhi-lin was Aide in the Secretariat of Jing province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhi-lin was an aide in the secretariat of Jing province.

sentences.zh: 仲威少有志氣，頗涉文史。

translations.literal: Zhongwei in youth had ambition and had read widely in letters and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwei in youth was ambitious and had read widely in letters and histories.

sentences.zh: 梁承聖中為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Under Liang's Chengsheng era he was Regular Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang's Chengsheng era he was regular attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 蕭莊偽署御史中丞，隨莊入齊，終於鄴中。

translations.literal: Zhuang's false regime made him Acting Censor-in-Chief; he followed Zhuang into Qi and died in Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang's puppet regime made him acting censor-in-chief. He followed Zhuang into Qi and died at Ye.

sentences.zh: 陸山才

translations.literal: Lu Shancai
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shancai

sentences.zh: 陸山才字孔章，吳郡吳人也。

translations.literal: Lu Shancai, styled Kongzhang, was a native of Wu in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shancai, styled Kongzhang, was a native of Wu in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖翁寶，梁尚書水部郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Wengbao was Liang Director of the Water Office in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Wengbao was Liang's director of the water office in the ministry of works.

sentences.zh: 父汎，散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His father Fan was Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fan was regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 紹泰中，都督周文育出鎮南豫州，不知書疏，乃以山才為長史，政事悉以委之。

translations.literal: In the Shaotai era Commander Zhou Wenyu went out to garrison South Yuzhou; he did not understand documents, and so he took Shancai as Chief Clerk and entrusted all administration to him.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shaotai era Commander Zhou Wenyu took up his post at South Yuzhou. Unable to manage documents himself, he made Shancai his chief clerk and left all administration to him.

sentences.zh: 文育南討，剋蕭勃，擒歐陽頠，計畫多出山才。

translations.literal: When Wenyu campaigned south he overcame Xiao Bo and captured Ouyang Yi; most of the plans came from Shancai.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenyu marched south he defeated Xiao Bo and captured Ouyang Yi; most of the plans were Shancai's.

sentences.zh: 及文育西征王琳，留山才監江州事，仍鎮豫章。

translations.literal: When Wenyu marched west against Wang Lin he left Shancai to oversee Jiangzhou affairs and still garrisoned Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenyu marched west against Wang Lin he left Shancai to oversee Jiangzhou and continued to hold Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 文育與侯安都於沌口敗績，余孝頃自新林來寇豫章，山才收合餘眾，依于周迪。

translations.literal: Wenyu with Hou Andu suffered defeat at Dundu; Yu Xiaoxu came from Xinlin to raid Yuzhang; Shancai gathered the remaining troops and attached himself to Zhou Di.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyu and Hou Andu were beaten at Dundu. Yu Xiaoxu came from Xinlin to strike Yuzhang. Shancai gathered the remnant army and joined Zhou Di.

sentences.zh: 擒余孝頃、李孝欽等，[9]遣山才自都陽之樂安嶺東道送于京師。

translations.literal: Yu Xiaoxu and Li Xiaoqin were captured; Editorial footnote marker 9. Zhou Di sent Shancai by the eastern route from Poyang through the Le'an Ridge to escort them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Di captured Yu Xiaoxu and Li Xiaoqin; [9] he sent Shancai by the eastern route from Poyang over the Le'an Ridge to deliver them to the capital.

sentences.zh: 除中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He was made Regular Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was made regular attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 復由樂安嶺綏撫南川諸郡。

translations.literal: Again by the Le'an Ridge he pacified the commanderies of the southern rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Again by way of the Le'an Ridge he pacified the southern river commanderies.

sentences.zh: 文育重鎮豫章金口，山才復為貞威將軍、鎮南長史、豫章太守。

translations.literal: Wenyu again held the Jin Ford of Yuzhang in force; Shancai was again made General of Manifest Prestige, Chief Clerk to the Pacifier of the South, and Administrator of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenyu again held the Jin Ford of Yuzhang in force, Shancai was again made general of manifest prestige, chief clerk to the pacifier of the south, and administrator of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 文育為熊曇朗所害，曇朗囚山才等，送于王琳。

translations.literal: Wenyu was killed by Xiong Tanlang; Tanlang imprisoned Shancai and the others and sent them to Wang Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyu was killed by Xiong Tanlang. Tanlang imprisoned Shancai and his party and sent them to Wang Lin.

sentences.zh: 未至，而侯安都敗琳將常眾愛於宮亭湖，由是山才獲反，除貞威將軍、新安太守。

translations.literal: Before they arrived, Hou Andu defeated Lin's general Chang Zhong'ai at Gongting Lake, and so Shancai was able to return; he was made General of Manifest Prestige and Administrator of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Before they arrived, Hou Andu defeated Lin's general Chang Zhong'ai at Gongting Lake, and Shancai was able to return. He was made general of manifest prestige and administrator of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 為王琳未平，留鎮富陽，以捍東道。

translations.literal: Because Lin was not yet pacified, he was left to garrison Fuyang to guard the eastern route.
translations.idiomatic: While Lin was still unbeaten he was left at Fuyang to guard the eastern line.

sentences.zh: 入為員外散騎常侍，遷宣惠始興王長史，行東揚州事。

translations.literal: He entered court as Supernumerary Regular Attendant and was promoted to Chief Clerk to the Prince of Shixing, Pacifier of the East, conducting office in East Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as supernumerary regular attendant and was promoted to chief clerk to the Prince of Shixing, pacifier of the east, acting in East Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 侯安都討留異，山才率王府之眾從焉。

translations.literal: When Hou Andu campaigned against Liu Yi, Shancai led the princely household troops with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Andu campaigned against Liu Yi, Shancai led the prince's household troops with him.

sentences.zh: 異平，除明威將軍、東陽太守。

translations.literal: When Yi was pacified, he was made General of Bright Prestige and Administrator of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Yi was subdued he was made general of bright prestige and administrator of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 入為鎮東始興王長史，帶會稽郡丞，行東揚州事。

translations.literal: He entered court as Chief Clerk to the Prince of Shixing, Pacifier of the East, concurrently Commandery Assistant of Kuaiji, conducting office in East Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as chief clerk to the Prince of Shixing, pacifier of the east, with Kuaiji commandery assistant, acting in East Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 未拜，改授散騎常侍，兼度支尚書，滿歲為真。

translations.literal: Before he took up the appointment he was changed to Regular Attendant, concurrently Acting Master of Revenue; after a full year he received the substantive post.
translations.idiomatic: Before he entered office he was reassigned to regular attendant and acting master of revenue; after a year he received the substantive appointment.

sentences.zh: 王質字子貞，右光祿大夫通之弟也。

translations.literal: Wang Zhi, styled Zizhen, was the younger brother of Right Grand Master of the Golden Sigil Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi, styled Zizhen, was the younger brother of right grand master of the golden sigil Tong.

sentences.zh: 少慷慨，涉獵書史。

translations.literal: In youth he was bold and generous and ranged widely in books and histories.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was bold and generous and read widely in books and histories.

sentences.zh: 梁世以武帝甥封甲口亭侯，補國子周易生，射策高第。

translations.literal: In Liang times, as Emperor Wu's sister's son he was enfeoffed Marquis of Jiakou ting, entered the National University as student of the Book of Changes, and ranked high in the archery examination.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang, as the emperor's sister's son, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jiakou and studied the Book of Changes at the national university, ranking high in the archery examination.

sentences.zh: 起家祕書郎、太子舍人、尚書殿中郎。

translations.literal: He began his career as Secretary, Household Retainer to the Heir Apparent, and Gentleman of the Palace Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He began as secretary, household retainer to the heir apparent, and gentleman of the palace hall.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂，居喪以孝聞。

translations.literal: On his mother's death he observed mourning and was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he mourned her and was known for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 服闋，除太子洗馬、東宮領直。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was made Mentor to the Heir Apparent and Leader of Direct Service in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was made mentor to the heir apparent and leader of direct service in the eastern palace.

sentences.zh: 累遷中舍人、庶子。

translations.literal: He rose through Household Retainer and Household Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through household retainer and household mentor.

sentences.zh: 太清元年，除假節、寧遠將軍，領東宮兵，從貞陽侯北伐。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiqing he was made Bearer of the Staff and General Who Pacifies the Distance and led the Eastern Palace troops in the Marquis of Zhenyang's northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taiqing (547) he was given the staff as General Who Pacifies the Distance, led the eastern palace troops on the Marquis of Zhenyang's northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 及貞陽敗績，質脫身逃還。

translations.literal: When Zhenyang was defeated, Zhi escaped and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenyang was beaten, Zhi slipped away and returned.

sentences.zh: 侯景於壽陽構逆，質又領舟師隨眾軍拒之。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled at Shouyang, Zhi again led the river forces with the massed armies to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled at Shouyang, Zhi again led the river fleet with the allied armies to block him.

sentences.zh: 景軍濟江，質便退走。

translations.literal: When Jing's army crossed the river, Zhi at once withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing's army crossed the Yangzi, Zhi at once fell back.

sentences.zh: 尋領步騎頓于宣陽門外。

translations.literal: Soon he led infantry and cavalry and encamped outside the Xuanyang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He soon led foot and horse and encamped outside the Xuanyang Gate.

sentences.zh: 景軍至京師，質不戰而潰，乃翦髮為桑門，潛匿人間。

translations.literal: When Jing's army reached the capital, Zhi did not fight and his troops collapsed; he then shaved his head as a monk and hid among the people.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing's army reached the capital, Zhi did not fight; his troops broke and he shaved his head as a monk and hid among the people.

sentences.zh: 及柳仲禮等會援京邑，軍據南岸，質又收合餘眾從之。

translations.literal: When Liu Zhongli and the others united to relieve the capital, the army held the south bank; Zhi again gathered the remaining troops and joined them.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zhongli and others united to relieve the capital, their army held the south bank. Zhi again gathered the remnant troops and joined them.

sentences.zh: 京城陷後，西奔荊州，元帝承制，以質為右長史，帶河東太守。

translations.literal: After the capital fell he fled west to Jingzhou; Emperor Yuan of Liang under the provisional regime made him Right Chief Clerk, concurrently Administrator of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital fell he fled west to Jingzhou. Emperor Yuan of Liang, under the provisional regime, made him right chief clerk and administrator of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 俄遷侍中。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 尋出為持節、都督吳州諸軍事、寧遠將軍、吳州刺史，領鄱陽內史。

translations.literal: Soon he went out as Bearer of the Staff, Commander of Military Affairs over Wu province, General Who Pacifies the Distance, and Inspector of Wu, concurrently Interior Magistrate of Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent out with the staff as commander of military affairs over Wu, General Who Pacifies the Distance, inspector of Wu, and interior magistrate of Poyang.

sentences.zh: 荊州陷，侯瑱鎮于湓城，與質不協，遣偏將羊亮代質，且以兵臨之，質率所部，度信安嶺，依于留異。

translations.literal: When Jing province fell, Hou Tian held Tangcheng and was at odds with Zhi; he sent a subordinate general, Yang Liang, to replace Zhi and also pressed him with troops; Zhi led his command over the Xin'an Ridge and attached himself to Liu Yi.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing province fell, Hou Tian held Tangcheng and clashed with Zhi. He sent the subordinate general Yang Liang to replace him and advanced with troops. Zhi led his command over the Xin'an Ridge and joined Liu Yi.

sentences.zh: 文帝鎮會稽，以兵助質，令鎮信安縣。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen garrisoned Kuaiji he sent troops to aid Zhi and had him hold Xin'an county.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen held Kuaiji he sent troops to aid Zhi and had him guard Xin'an county.

sentences.zh: 永定二年，高祖命質率所部踰嶺出豫章，隨都督周文育以討王琳。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongding the Founder ordered Zhi to lead his command over the ridge into Yuzhang and follow Commander Zhou Wenyu against Wang Lin.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongding (558) the Founder ordered Zhi to lead his command over the mountains into Yuzhang and follow Commander Zhou Wenyu against Wang Lin.

sentences.zh: 質與琳素善，或譖云於軍中潛信交通，高祖命周文育殺質，文育啟請救之，獲免。

translations.literal: Zhi and Lin had long been on good terms; some slandered him, saying that in the army he secretly corresponded with Lin; the Founder ordered Zhou Wenyu to kill Zhi; Wenyu memorialized to plead for his life, and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi and Lin had long been friends. Some accused him of secret correspondence with Lin in the field. The Founder ordered Zhou Wenyu to execute him; Wenyu pleaded for his life and he was spared.

sentences.zh: 尋授散騎常侍、晉陵太守。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Regular Attendant and Administrator of Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made regular attendant and administrator of Jinling.

sentences.zh: 文帝嗣位，徵守五兵尚書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded he was summoned to hold the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen succeeded he was recalled to head the ministry of war.

sentences.zh: 高宗為揚州刺史，以質為仁威將軍、驃騎府長史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan was Inspector of Yangzhou he made Zhi General of Benevolent Prestige and Chief Clerk to the Flying Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan was inspector of Yangzhou he made Zhi general of benevolent prestige and chief clerk to the flying cavalry.

sentences.zh: 天嘉二年，除晉安太守。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiancheng he was made Administrator of Jin'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tiancheng (561) he was made administrator of Jin'an.

sentences.zh: 高宗輔政，以為司徒左長史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan served as regent he made Zhi Left Chief Clerk of the Secretariat, general unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan was regent he made Zhi left chief clerk of the Secretariat, retaining his general's title.

sentences.zh: 坐公事免官。

translations.literal: He was dismissed from office for a public matter.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed for an offense in public business.

sentences.zh: 尋為通直散騎常侍，遷太府卿、都官尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Regular Attendant of Direct Communication, promoted to Grand Steward and Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made regular attendant of direct communication and promoted to grand steward and minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 太建二年卒，時年六十。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taijian he died, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taijian (570) he died, aged sixty.

sentences.zh: 贈本官，諡曰安子。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given his former office; posthumous name Anzi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously given his former rank, with the posthumous name Anzi.

sentences.zh: 韋載字德基，京兆杜陵人也。

translations.literal: Wei Zai, styled Deji, was a native of Duling in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zai, styled Deji, was a native of Duling in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 祖叡，梁開府儀同三司，永昌嚴公。

translations.literal: His grandfather Rui was a Liang Opener of the Mansion Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes and Duke Yan of Yongchang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Rui had been a Liang opener of the mansion equal in honor to the three dukes and Duke Yan of Yongchang.

sentences.zh: 父政，[10]梁黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: His father Zheng, [10] a Liang Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zheng [10] had been a Liang attendant of the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 載少聰惠，篤志好學。

translations.literal: Zai from youth was clever and keen, with a steadfast will and love of learning.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Zai was bright and eager, devoted to study.

sentences.zh: 年十二，隨叔父稜見沛國劉顯，顯問漢書十事，載隨問應答，曾無疑滯。

translations.literal: At age twelve, following his uncle Ling he saw Liu Xian of Pei; Xian asked ten matters from the Book of Han, and Zai answered each question as it came, never hesitating or stumbling.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he went with his uncle Ling to see Liu Xian of Pei. Xian quizzed him on ten points from the Book of Han; Zai answered on the spot without a pause.

sentences.zh: 及長，博涉文史，沉敏有器局。

translations.literal: When grown, he ranged widely through letters and histories, was deep and keen, and had capacity and judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Grown up, he was widely read in letters and history, thoughtful and quick, with real judgment.

sentences.zh: 起家梁邵陵王法曹參軍，遷太子舍人、尚書三公郎。

translations.literal: He first entered office as a Liang legal aide to the Prince of Shaoling, was transferred to Crown Prince Attendant and Gentleman of the Three Dukes in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He began as legal aide to the prince of Shaoling under Liang, then became crown prince attendant and gentleman of the three dukes in the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，元帝承制以為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion, Emperor Yuan of Liang, assuming the provisional regime, made him Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion Emperor Yuan of Liang, ruling provisionally, made him attendant of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 尋為建威將軍、尋陽太守，隨都督王僧辯東討侯景。

translations.literal: Soon he became General Who Establishes Might and Administrator of Xunyang, following the area commander Wang Sengbian east to attack Hou Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made general who establishes might and administrator of Xunyang, marching east under Wang Sengbian against Hou Jing.

sentences.zh: 是時僧辯軍于湓城，而魯悉達、樊俊等各擁兵保境，觀望成敗。

translations.literal: At that time Sengbian's army was at Pencheng, while Lu Sidada, Fan Jun, and others each held troops guarding their borders, watching the outcome.
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian then lay at Pencheng; Lu Sidada, Fan Jun, and others each held their districts with troops and waited to see who would win.

sentences.zh: 元帝以載為假節、都督太原高唐新蔡三郡諸軍事、高唐太守。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan made Zai Acting with Staff, Area Commander over Military Affairs in the three commanderies of Taiyuan, Gaotang, and Xincai, and Administrator of Gaotang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan made Zai acting commander with staff over Taiyuan, Gaotang, and Xincai and administrator of Gaotang.

sentences.zh: 仍銜命喻悉達等令出軍討景。

translations.literal: He still bore orders to persuade Sidada and the others to take the field and attack Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He was also charged to win Sidada and the rest over and bring them out against Hou Jing.

sentences.zh: 及大軍東下，載率三郡兵自焦湖出柵口，與僧辯會于梁山。

translations.literal: When the great army marched east, Zai led the troops of the three commanderies out from Jiao Lake through Shankou and joined Sengbian at Mount Liang.
translations.idiomatic: When the main force moved east, Zai led the three commanderies' men from Jiao Lake through Shankou to meet Sengbian at Mount Liang.

sentences.zh: 景平，除冠軍將軍、琅邪太守。

translations.literal: When Jing was pacified, he was made General Who Champions and Administrator of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing fell he was made champion general and administrator of Langye.

sentences.zh: 尋奉使往東陽、晉安，招撫留異、陳寶應等。

translations.literal: Soon he was sent on mission to Dongyang and Jin'an to win over and pacify Liu Yi, Chen Baoying, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent to Dongyang and Jin'an to bring Liu Yi, Chen Baoying, and others over.

sentences.zh: 仍授信武將軍、義興太守。

translations.literal: He was then made Trustworthy Martial General and Administrator of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made trustworthy-martial general and administrator of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 高祖誅王僧辯，乃遣周文育輕兵襲載，未至而載先覺，乃嬰城自守。

translations.literal: The Founder executed Wang Sengbian and then sent Zhou Wenyü with light troops to strike Zai; before they arrived Zai had already sensed it and walled the city to hold out.
translations.idiomatic: After the Founder killed Wang Sengbian he sent Zhou Wenyü with light troops against Zai. Zai saw it coming first and shut the city to resist.

sentences.zh: 文育攻之甚急，載所屬縣卒並高祖舊兵，多善用弩，載收得數十人，繫以長鎖，命所親監之，使射文育軍，約曰十發不兩中者則死，每發輒中，所中皆斃。

translations.literal: Wenyü pressed the attack fiercely; the district soldiers under Zai were all the Founder's old troops and many were skilled with crossbows. Zai gathered several dozen men, bound them with long chains, had those he trusted supervise them, and made them shoot at Wenyü's army, stipulating that any who failed to hit twice in ten shots would die; every shot struck, and all who were hit fell dead.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyü attacked hard. Zai's county levies were many of the Founder's old soldiers and crack crossbowmen. He took several dozen, chained them in a row, set trusted men over them, and made them shoot at Wenyü's host on pain of death if they missed twice in ten tries. Every bolt found its mark and every man hit went down.

sentences.zh: 文育軍稍卻，因於城外據水立柵，相持數旬。

translations.literal: Wenyü's army gradually fell back; he therefore took the water outside the city and set up a palisade, and they faced each other for several tens of days.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyü's men gave ground. He threw up a river palisade outside the walls, and the two sides stood off for weeks.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞文育軍不利，乃自將征之，剋其水柵。

translations.literal: The Founder heard that Wenyü's army was faring ill and then personally led a campaign against him, storming the water palisade.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Wenyü was losing, the Founder came in person, stormed the river camp, and broke it.

sentences.zh: 仍遣載族弟翽賷書喻載以誅王僧辯意，并奉梁敬帝敕，〔敕〕載解兵。

translations.literal: He then sent Zai's clansman Hui bearing a letter to explain to Zai the reason for executing Wang Sengbian, and also presented an edict of Emperor Jing of Liang, [edict] ordering Zai to disarm.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Zai's cousin Hui with a letter explaining why Wang Sengbian had been killed and with an edict from Emperor Jing of Liang ordering Zai to lay down arms.

sentences.zh: [11]載得書，乃以其眾降于高祖。

translations.literal: [11] When Zai received the letter, he thereupon led his troops in surrender to the Founder.
translations.idiomatic: [11] Zai opened the letter and surrendered with his force to the Founder.

sentences.zh: 高祖厚加撫慰，即以其族弟翽監義興郡，所部將帥，並隨才任使，引載恆置左右，與之謀議。

translations.literal: The Founder greatly comforted and reassured him, immediately put his clansman Hui in charge of Yixing commandery, assigned all the generals and officers under him according to their talents, and kept Zai always at his side to consult with him.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder treated him generously, set his cousin Hui over Yixing, placed his officers each where he could best use them, and kept Zai at his side for counsel.

sentences.zh: 徐嗣徽、任約等引齊軍濟江，據石頭城，高祖問計於載，載曰：「齊軍若分兵先據三吳之路，略地東境，則時事去矣。

translations.literal: Xu Sihui, Ren Yue, and others brought Qi troops across the river and held Stone City; the Founder asked Zai for a plan, and Zai said: "If the Qi army divides its forces and first seizes the roads of the Three Wu, overrunning the eastern borderlands, then the times are lost.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Sihui and Ren Yue brought Qi troops across the Yangzi and held Stone City. The Founder asked Zai's advice. Zai said, "If Qi splits its army and first takes the routes through the Three Wu and raids the east, the cause is lost.

sentences.zh: 今可急於淮南即侯景故壘築城，以通東道轉輸，別命輕兵絕其糧運，使進無所虜，退無所資，則齊將之首，旬日可致。

translations.literal: Now we should quickly build a city on the Huai at Hou Jing's old rampart to open the eastern supply route, and separately order light troops to cut their grain transport, so that advancing they have nothing to seize and retreating they have nothing to rely on—then the heads of the Qi generals can be had within ten days."
translations.idiomatic: We should hurry to build a fort on the Huai at Hou Jing's old site to keep the eastern line open, and send light troops to cut their supplies so they cannot feed an advance or a retreat. Then the Qi commanders' heads will be ours within ten days."

sentences.zh: 」高祖從其計。

translations.literal: The Founder followed his plan.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder took his advice.

sentences.zh: 天嘉元年，以疾去官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjia he left office because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjia year one he resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 載有田十餘頃，在江乘縣之白山，至是遂築室而居，屏絕人事，吉凶慶弔，無所往來，不入籬門者幾十載。

translations.literal: Zai had fields of more than ten qing at White Mountain in Jiangcheng county; at this he built a dwelling and lived there, cutting himself off from human affairs; for joys and sorrows, congratulations and condolences, he went nowhere and for nearly ten years did not pass his hedge gate.
translations.idiomatic: He owned more than ten qing of land at White Mountain in Jiangcheng and now built a house there, shut out the world, and for nearly ten years never crossed his gate for feast or funeral.

sentences.zh: 太建中卒於家，時年五十八。

translations.literal: In the Taijian era he died at home, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home in the Taijian era, aged fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 族弟翽

translations.literal: Clansman Hui
translations.idiomatic: Clansman Hui

sentences.zh: 子宏，字德禮，有文學，歷官至永嘉王府諮議參軍。

translations.literal: His son Hong, courtesy name Deli, had literary talent and rose in office to Aide to the Prince of Yongjia.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hong, styled Deli, was a man of letters and rose to aide in the household of the prince of Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 陳亡入隋。

translations.literal: When Chen perished he entered Sui.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell he entered Sui service.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：昔鄧禹基於文學，杜預出自儒雅，卒致軍功，名著前代。

translations.literal: The historian says: In old times Deng Yu rose from literary study and Du Yu came out of refined Confucian learning, yet in the end they achieved military merit and their fame stands in former ages.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Deng Yu began in the classics and Du Yu in pure scholarship, yet both won fame in war and live in the histories of old.

sentences.zh: 晉氏喪亂，播遷江左，顧榮、郗鑒之輩，溫嶠、謝玄之倫，莫非巾褐書生，搢紳素譽，抗敵以衛社稷，立勳而升台鼎。

translations.literal: When the Jin house fell into disorder and was driven east across the river, men such as Gu Rong and Xi Jian, and the likes of Wen Jiao and Xie Xuan, were all plain-clothed scholars of gentry repute who resisted the enemy to guard the altars of state and by merit rose to the highest offices.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin collapsed and fled to the south, Gu Rong and Xi Jian, Wen Jiao and Xie Xuan, were scholar-gentry in plain dress who took up arms for the realm and by merit reached the highest posts.

sentences.zh: 自斯以降，代有其人。

translations.literal: From that time down, each age has had such men.
translations.idiomatic: Since then every age has produced men of that kind.

sentences.zh: 但梁室沸騰，懦夫立志，既身逢際會，見仗於時主，美矣！

translations.literal: Yet when the Liang house seethed, cowards found resolve; having themselves met the moment and being trusted by the rulers of the day—how fine!
translations.idiomatic: When Liang boiled with war even timid men found their nerve; they met their hour and were armed by their lords—worthy of praise indeed.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation notes

sentences.zh: 賦成奏帝善之手敕答曰 按北監本、汲本、殿本及《南史沈約傳》附眾傳並作「賦成奏之，帝手敕答曰」。

translations.literal: When the fu was finished he presented it; the emperor was pleased and replied by hand—comment: the Northern Supervisory, Ji, Palace, and Hall editions and the attached biography of Shen Zhong in the History of the Southern Dynasties all read "when the fu was finished he presented it; the emperor replied by hand, saying."
translations.idiomatic: On "when the fu was finished he presented it; the emperor was pleased and replied by hand": Northern Supervisory, Ji, Palace, and Hall editions and Shen Zhong's biography in the Southern Dynasties history read "presented it; the emperor replied by hand, saying."

sentences.zh: 及景圍臺城 「圍臺」二字原本墨丁，據各本補。

translations.literal: When Jing besieged the Terrace City—the two characters "besieged the Terrace" were originally effaced in the base text and are now supplied from the various editions.
translations.idiomatic: On "when Jing besieged the Terrace City": wei tai was faded in the base text and is restored from other editions.

sentences.zh: 朝士共誚其所為 「士」字原本墨丁，據各本補。

translations.literal: The court gentlemen together mocked his conduct—the character "gentlemen" was originally effaced in the base text and is now supplied from the various editions.
translations.idiomatic: On "the court gentlemen together mocked his conduct": shi was faded in the base text and is restored from other editions.

sentences.zh: 及莊僭立 「僭」字原本墨丁，據各本補。

translations.literal: When Zhuang usurped the throne—the character "usurped" was originally effaced in the base text and is now supplied from the various editions.
translations.idiomatic: On "when Zhuang usurped the throne": jian was faded in the base text and is restored from other editions.

sentences.zh: 以泌為侍中丞相長史 「丞」字原本墨丁，據各本補。

translations.literal: Made Mi Attendant-in-Ordinary and Chief Clerk of the Chancellor—the character "chancellor" was originally effaced in the base text and is now supplied from the various editions.
translations.idiomatic: On "made Mi attendant-in-ordinary and chief clerk of the chancellor": cheng was faded in the base text and is restored from other editions.

sentences.zh: 琳軍敗 「軍敗」二字原本墨丁，據各本補。

translations.literal: Lin's army was defeated—the two characters "army defeated" were originally effaced in the base text and are now supplied from the various editions.
translations.idiomatic: On "Lin's army was defeated": jun bai was faded in the base text and is restored from other editions.

sentences.zh: 臨終戒其子蔓華曰 「蔓華」《南史》作「芳華」。

translations.literal: On his deathbed he admonished his son Manhua, saying—"Manhua" in the History of the Southern Dynasties reads "Fanghua."
translations.idiomatic: On "on his deathbed he admonished his son Manhua": the Southern Dynasties history reads Fanghua.

sentences.zh: 范陽張

translations.literal: Fanyang Zhang
translations.idiomatic: Fanyang Zhang

translations.literal: (continued)
translations.idiomatic: (continued)

sentences.zh: 〔纘〕據《南史》改，下同。

translations.literal: [Juan]—changed according to the History of the Southern Dynasties; the same below.
translations.idiomatic: [Juan]—emended per the Southern Dynasties history; the same below.

sentences.zh: 按張纘，《梁書》、《南史》並有傳。

translations.literal: Comment: Zhang Juan has biographies in both the Book of Liang and the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Juan has biographies in the Book of Liang and the Southern Dynasties history.

sentences.zh: 本書

translations.literal: This book
translations.idiomatic: This book

sentences.zh: 〈王勱傳〉

translations.literal: 〈Biography of Wang Li〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Biography of Wang Li〉

sentences.zh: 亦有「范陽張纘」之語。

translations.literal: also has the phrase "Zhang Juan of Fanyang."
translations.idiomatic: also has the phrase "Zhang Juan of Fanyang."

sentences.zh: 擒余孝頃李孝欽等 按「擒」字上當補「周迪」二字，文義方足。

translations.literal: Captured Yu Xiaopin, Li Xiaoqin, and others—comment: above "captured" the two characters "Zhou Di" should be supplied; only then is the sense complete.
translations.idiomatic: On "captured Yu Xiaopin and Li Xiaoqin": the name Zhou Di is missing before "captured" and should be supplied.

sentences.zh: 父政 「政」《梁書》、《南史》

translations.literal: Father Zheng—the graph zheng (govern) in the Book of Liang and the History of the Southern Dynasties
translations.idiomatic: On "father Zheng": the Book of Liang and the History of the Southern Dynasties read the graph zheng (govern).

sentences.zh: 〈韋叡傳〉

translations.literal: 〈Biography of Wei Rui〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Biography of Wei Rui〉

sentences.zh: 作「正」。

translations.literal: Has "Zheng" (upright/correct).
translations.idiomatic: The text reads zheng (upright/correct).

sentences.zh: 〔敕〕載解兵 據北監本、汲本、殿本及《南史》補。

translations.literal: [edict] ordering Zai to disarm—supplied according to the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Palace editions and the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: On "[edict] ordering Zai to disarm": supplied from Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Palace editions and the Southern Dynasties history.
